description: Op application (SCREENS.md §4.2) and live frames (§4.1). Each case starts from a document's state (`document`: "base" is the file's `base` document, a fixture path under fixtures/, or inline), applies each step in turn (a list of ops, {"frame": ...} for a socket frame, or {"poll": ...} for a poll answer) and must reach `state`: id'd parts flat with their own properties (children, and child, template, empty, fallback and overlay when they hold a part, left out; a tabs part's tabs without their child), collections as held, `drawn` (each collection's keys as drawn: those in `order` that have an item, then the rest sorted by key), chart points per mark, toasts and reload. A snap frame, and a poll answer with snap: true, apply to the document's own state.

cases.note: the state a renderer starts from: id'd parts flat with their own properties (no children), template ids not indexed, chart points per mark; a spectrum's overlay flag is a property, a video's overlay part is a child
a new key is drawn after those in `order` until an `order` names it
a removed key leaves `order` too, so an `up` that brings it back draws it last
kept as sent; a key with no item is not drawn
items missing from `order` are drawn last, sorted by key
push to a missing item is ignored
the new part keeps the id it replaces
a `snap` (after a reconnect) is applied to the document's own state, not on top of what was held
a poll answer without `snap` applies on top; with `snap: true` it is the whole state, applied to the document's state, so a polled screen drops items without remembering what it sent
